back: Map config addresses to real IDs; record dependencies/metadata; cache attributes for performance; know what to destroy when blocks are removed.
`serial` increments on every write (detects stale copies). `lineage` is a UUID set when the state was created (detects unrelated states).

front: What is drift and how do you handle it?
back: Real infrastructure changed outside Terraform. Revert it with a normal apply, or accept it by updating code (optionally `apply -refresh-only` to record observed values).
Shows changes made outside Terraform without proposing infrastructure changes. `apply -refresh-only` writes the observed values into state. Replaced `terraform refresh`.
`use_lockfile = true`: Terraform creates `<key>.tflock` with a conditional PutObject (`If-None-Match`). GA in 1.11. `dynamodb_table` is deprecated.
Leave `backend "s3" {}` empty in code and pass settings with `terraform init -backend-config=prod.s3.tfbackend`. Needed because backend blocks can't use variables.
`-migrate-state` copies existing state into the new backend. `-reconfigure` uses the new backend settings without copying anything.

front: How to clear a stale lock
back: Confirm nobody is running Terraform, then `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>`. Never `-lock=false`. Use `-lock-timeout=5m` to wait for real locks in CI.

`moved { from = OLD  to = NEW }` changes an object's address in state through the normal plan: renames, moving into modules, switching to count/for_each. Keep it until all states have applied it (forever in shared modules).
`import { to = ADDR  id = "provider-id" }` adopts an existing object via plan/apply (1.5+). `terraform plan -generate-config-out=gen.tf` drafts the config (experimental).
`removed { from = ADDR  lifecycle { destroy = false } }` forgets an object without destroying it (1.7+). Config-driven version of `terraform state rm`.
Forces destroy+create of one resource in the plan. Supersedes `terraform taint`.
Get the previous version (local `.backup` or versioned bucket), check lineage/serial with `jq`, then `terraform state push` (bump serial or `-force` deliberately).

front: Settings to use the S3 backend with MinIO-compatible servers
Plan says it will create something that already exists. Why and fix?
back: The object fell out of state (e.g. `state rm`, lost state). Re-adopt it with an `import` block instead of letting apply fail on a name conflict.
